What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We map how bookings, trips, receipts, documents, exceptions, PODs and settlements actually flow, sit with the booking desk, control tower, hub, warehouse, fleet and billing teams, and pick the workflows where automation helps most. We baseline KPIs from TMS, WMS, GPS and accounting data and identify GST, customs, messaging and personal data boundaries early.

    Deliverables

    • Current-state maps for the selected workflows
    • Data source inventory covering TMS, WMS, GPS, forwarding software, accounts and portals
    • Prioritized automation backlog with effort and risk
    • KPI baseline and measurement plan

    What we need from you

    • Read access or sample exports from the TMS, WMS, GPS platform and accounts
    • Time with booking, control-tower, hub, warehouse, fleet and billing staff
    • Customer contracts, SLAs, rate cards and approval matrices
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design each workflow with its triggers, data fields, decision rules, approval points and failure paths, plus the WhatsApp and SMS templates, driver and rider flows and review screens people will use. We agree which actions stay with authorized users, such as e-way bill extensions and customs filings, and how consent is collected for consignee and driver messages.

    Deliverables

    • Workflow designs with human checkpoints and exception paths
    • Integration plan for TMS, WMS, GPS, GSP, forwarding and messaging systems
    • WhatsApp, SMS and driver-app message designs
    • Access, consent and retention design

    What we need from you

    • Rate, claims, remittance and expense rules approved by their owners
    • Consignee and driver notice and consent wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • Confirmation from the customs broker and tax advisor of the steps that stay with them
  3. 3

    Build

    2–6 weeks

    We build integrations, workflows, review screens and dashboards in a test environment using sample or masked data, with logging, alerts and role-based access from the start. Each workflow is demonstrated to its owners with real scenarios from their lanes, hubs and clients as it takes shape.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows in a test environment
    • TMS, WMS, GPS, accounting and WhatsApp integrations
    • Review and approval screens for pricing, billing, fleet and NDR teams
    • Dashboards built on the agreed KPI definitions
    • Run logs, alerts and error handling

    What we need from you

    • API credentials or service accounts with least-privilege access
    • WhatsApp Business account verification, template submissions and DLT template registration
    • Test data and named testers from each team
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    Owners test each workflow against real situations: failed deliveries with disputed reasons, partial receipts, rollovers, expiring e-way bills, short COD deposits and unreadable PODs. We launch with one branch, hub, client, port or lane first, run alongside the current process for a short period, and train approvers and exception handlers.

    Deliverables

    • User acceptance results signed off by owners
    • Parallel-run comparison with the current process
    • Training for approvers, agents and exception handlers
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Named owners to sign off each workflow
    • A pilot branch, hub, client, port or lane
    • Communication to drivers, riders, merchants or clients about the change
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    We monitor runs, failures, message delivery and AI accuracy, review KPIs with owners each month, tune rules, thresholds and prompts, and add workflows from the backlog. Changes to rate cards, SLAs, portals or regulations follow the same design, test and approval route as the original build.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and exception review
    • Sampled AI accuracy checks with prompt and rule updates
    • Incident log with fixes and preventive actions
    • Updated backlog and roadmap

    What we need from you

    • Monthly review time with the business owner
    • Feedback from agents, drivers, riders and clients
    • Advance notice of new clients, contracts, rate cards or system changes

First pilot: Exception and NDR pilot for one hub, region or lane

A four to six week pilot that connects tracking events for one hub, region or lane, flags delays and failed deliveries, sends approved consignee updates and NDR choices, and gives the control tower one exception queue. Forwarders can pilot the customs checklist for one port instead, and fleets the document register with e-way bill alerts. We compare results with the baseline and decide together whether to extend.

  • Milestone feed from the TMS or courier platform and GPS for one hub, region or lane
  • Delay, no-movement and failed-delivery rules with owners and deadlines
  • Approved WhatsApp and DLT-registered SMS templates for delay updates and NDR choices
  • Write-back of re-attempt instructions and an exception queue for the control tower
  • KPI comparison with the baseline, followed by a go or no-go review

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • The TMS, WMS, forwarding software and accounts stay the systems of record. Automations write only agreed instructions, drafts or status fields, and never generate e-way bills, file customs declarations or post invoices without a named authorized user.
  • A written approval matrix names who decides rates, margins, claims, credit notes, remittances, expense deductions, returns and driver or rider eligibility, and every approval is logged against that person.
  • Consignee, driver and rider data is minimized: masked numbers and addresses where platforms allow, consent and opt-out records, role-based access, retention periods per data type, and breach steps designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.
  • Customer messages use approved WhatsApp templates and DLT-registered SMS service templates, carry no promotions unless the person agreed to them, and never promise compensation, refunds or delivery times the operations team has not confirmed.
  • AI output is labeled as a draft or classification with links to its source data, low-confidence cases go to people, and samples are checked for accuracy every month.
  • Every workflow has run logs, failure alerts, an exception owner and a rollback plan, and credentials sit in a secrets vault with least-privilege, read-only access wherever writing is not needed.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • GST e-way bills: validity, Part B and extensions (CGST Rule 138)

    Goods worth more than ₹50,000 per consignment generally move with an e-way bill. Validity runs one day per 200 km, or per 20 km for over-dimensional cargo; Part B must be updated before goods change vehicles; and the transporter in charge may extend validity from eight hours before to eight hours after expiry. Since January 2025, the portal rejects bills on documents older than 180 days and extensions beyond 360 days. GSTN revises portal rules by advisory.

    taxinformation.cbic.gov.in · Source

  • Motor Vehicles Act and CMVR documents for vehicles and drivers

    When asked, drivers must produce a license of the right class, the registration certificate, insurance and PUC certificate, plus the fitness certificate and permit for transport vehicles. Rule 139 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, amended in 2018, accepts these in electronic form, and MoRTH's procedure recognizes DigiLocker and mParivahan copies. Workflows take expiry dates from the documents and VAHAN or SARATHI records, and the fleet manager decides exceptions.

    morth.gov.in · Source

  • Customs filing on ICEGATE and Bill of Entry timelines

    Bills of Entry and shipping bills are filed on ICEGATE by the importer, exporter or a licensed customs broker, with supporting documents uploaded through e-Sanchit. Under Section 46 of the Customs Act as amended in 2021, a Bill of Entry is generally due before the end of the day preceding arrival; the Board may allow later limits in some cases, and late filing without sufficient cause attracts charges. Automations track checklists and status; the broker files and signs.

    old.cbic.gov.in · Source

  • Carriage by Road Act, 2007 for common carriers

    Businesses that collect, store, forward or deliver goods by road for hire, including booking agents and courier agencies, need a certificate of registration as a common carrier. The consignor executes a goods forwarding note declaring the value and any dangerous or hazardous goods, and the carrier issues a goods receipt; liability follows these documents. Booking flows can capture the declaration and produce the documents, with exceptions reviewed by the booking desk.

    indiacode.nic.in · Source

  • Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025

    Consignees, merchants' customers, drivers and riders are data principals. The DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases: consent manager provisions from November 2026 and most duties, including notice, consent, security safeguards, breach intimation and erasure, from May 2027. MeitY has consulted on bringing dates forward, so we design for them now. Merchant and brand contracts name the data fiduciary and the processor. GDPR may apply to EU contacts.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • Messaging consent on WhatsApp, SMS and calls

    WhatsApp requires an opt-in that names the business, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and a clear path to a person in automated chats, and since January 2026 Meta bars general-purpose AI assistants, so ours answer only about the client's shipments. SMS and calls follow TRAI's TCCCPR, amended in February 2025 and September 2026: DLT-registered headers and templates, with delivery and NDR updates sent as service messages without promotions.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

Frequently asked

Do we need to replace our TMS, WMS or forwarding software?

No. Your TMS or courier platform, WMS, forwarding software and accounts stay the systems of record. We connect through their APIs, webhooks, EDI or scheduled exports and write back only agreed fields, such as re-attempt instructions, exception status or draft invoices. Where a system has no API, we start with exports and agree a path to a sturdier integration.

Will the automation generate or extend e-way bills or file customs declarations?

No. Workflows read e-way bill and customs status, alert the right people and prepare the details. An authorized user at your company submits e-way bill extensions and Part B updates, and your licensed customs broker classifies, values, files and signs declarations on ICEGATE.

Can we send delivery updates and NDR choices on WhatsApp?

Yes, through the WhatsApp Business Platform via Meta or an approved provider, to consignees who opted in to messages from the sender, for example at a merchant checkout that names the courier, or from the merchant's own WhatsApp account. Messages outside the 24-hour customer service window use templates approved by WhatsApp. Without a WhatsApp opt-in, the same choices go by SMS on DLT-registered service templates. Messages carry no promotions and every opt-out is honored.

How do you protect consignee, driver and rider data?

We collect only the fields each workflow needs, mask phone numbers and addresses for riders and agents where the platform allows, keep documents encrypted with role-based access, and agree retention periods per data type. Contracts with merchants and clients set out who acts as data fiduciary and who as processor, and notices, consent records and breach response steps are designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.

Will AI decide claims, deductions or driver eligibility?

No. AI reads documents, classifies replies, drafts quotes and invoices, and answers tracking questions from your data. Pricing leads approve rates, finance approves invoices, remittances and settlements, fleet and HR managers decide driver and rider eligibility and any deduction, and claims owners decide claims. Every approval is logged against a named person.

Does this work with attached market vehicles, not just our own fleet?

Yes. Document collection and expiry tracking work for attached vehicles and their owners, and POD and expense capture run on WhatsApp, so drivers need no extra app. Where GPS is not fitted, location can come from consent-based phone tracking or FASTag toll crossings where your ULIP access includes them. Vehicle and license checks use VAHAN and SARATHI records with the owner's and driver's consent.

How long before something is live?

A first pilot usually takes four to six weeks from discovery to a working workflow for one hub, lane, client or port, depending on access to systems and how quickly approval rules and message templates are agreed. Larger workflows such as RFQ-to-quote or the tracking assistant are delivered in stages.

How do you measure whether it worked?

We baseline the agreed KPIs during Discover, such as first-attempt delivery rate, exception resolution time, POD-to-invoice time or quote turnaround, and review them with you every month after launch. We do not promise fixed improvements in advance; the numbers come from your own data.
